trigger.reason: An existing strategy course needs a new applied thread without discarding a coherent diagnostic and choice sequence.
inspectedEvidence: Approved strategy course outline and session notes
Participant case submissions from two prior deliveries
Sponsor brief requesting faster review and revision practice

programme.subject: Strategy as diagnosis, choice, coordinated action, and revision
programme.scope: A six-session course that preserves the existing strategic core while strengthening implementation and review
programme.audience: Business-unit leaders who contribute to strategy but do not work as specialist strategists
programme.startingPoint: Learners can describe goals and initiatives but often leave the governing diagnosis and rejected alternatives implicit

thesis.recognisedProblem: The existing course produces credible strategic choices but its final exercises do not show how assumptions will be monitored and revised.
thesis.promisedLearnerChange: Learners leave able to defend one strategic choice, connect it to coordinated action, and specify the evidence that would trigger revision.
thesis.centralQuestion: How can a strategy remain coherent while becoming easier to challenge and revise?
thesis.distinctiveArgument: A strategy becomes usable when diagnosis, choice, action, and revision share one visible chain of reasoning.
thesis.argumentBoundary: The course develops the reasoning architecture of a strategy and does not substitute for industry modelling or specialist financial analysis.
thesis.changedCondition: The sponsor now needs leaders to revisit strategic assumptions during execution rather than only at the annual planning cycle.

sources.label: Participant case pack and completed assignments

audit.originalPurpose: Require learners to explain the obstacle before choosing an aspiration or initiative.
audit.enduringRequirementOrFunction: A strategic choice still needs a causal account of the obstacle it is meant to overcome.
audit.inheritedForm: An opening case comparison followed by a written diagnosis of the learner's own business situation.
audit.changedCondition: The new brief changes review frequency but does not remove the need for a governing diagnosis.
audit.authorClaimOrSynthesis: The opening diagnosis sequence remains the right foundation for every later commitment in the course.
audit.dispositionReason: Prior submissions show that the sequence exposes assumptions that remain necessary for choice and later revision.
audit.programmeFit: Retains the opening capability and supplies the baseline against which changing evidence can be interpreted.
audit.learnerMove: Learners write a causal diagnosis before naming their preferred initiative.
audit.artifactProof: The strategy record begins with an obstacle and causal explanation rather than a goal list.

audit.originalPurpose: Make strategy selective by recording what the organisation will not pursue.
audit.enduringRequirementOrFunction: Scarce attention and resources still make trade-offs unavoidable.
audit.inheritedForm: A decision table comparing three strategic alternatives against the diagnosis.
audit.changedCondition: More frequent review changes when a choice may be reopened, not the need to make one.
audit.authorClaimOrSynthesis: The explicit comparison should remain intact and acquire a later revision threshold.
audit.dispositionReason: The comparison already performs essential selection work and can accept the new threshold without structural replacement.
audit.programmeFit: Keeps the course selective while linking each rejected option to evidence that could reopen it.
audit.learnerMove: Learners choose among plausible alternatives and state why the others remain rejected.
audit.artifactProof: The strategy record contains one selected option, two rejected options, and their decision criteria.

audit.originalPurpose: Translate strategic choice into reinforcing actions and expose contradictions through participant cases.
audit.enduringRequirementOrFunction: A strategy still depends on actions that reinforce rather than cancel one another.
audit.inheritedForm: Separate implementation lecture and end-of-course participant case presentation.
audit.changedCondition: The new brief requires assumptions and review thresholds to travel with coordinated actions during execution.
audit.authorClaimOrSynthesis: Implementation and case application should become one working session that attaches review evidence to each coordinated action.
audit.dispositionReason: Joining the lecture and case work lets learners test coordination and revision on the same strategic record instead of transferring between two artifacts.
audit.programmeFit: Creates the bridge from strategic choice to monitored action without altering the inherited diagnostic core.
audit.learnerMove: Learners attach owners, reinforcing actions, assumptions, and revision evidence to the selected strategy.
audit.artifactProof: The final strategy record shows how each action supports the choice and what evidence would reopen it.

transformationLens.reason: Most of the inherited architecture remains sound, while the review cycle changes the form in which assumptions and implementation evidence must travel.
transformationLens.governingQuestion: What must remain coherent when strategic review moves from an annual event into ongoing execution?

evidenceBoundaries.claim: Prior final exercises rarely specified the evidence that would cause learners to revise their selected strategy.
evidenceBoundaries.attribution: Programme author's review of participant submissions
evidenceBoundaries.observedScope: Twenty-four final submissions from two deliveries of the existing six-session course
evidenceBoundaries.known: Most submissions named initiatives but omitted explicit revision thresholds.
evidenceBoundaries.uncertain: The submissions do not show whether learners used undocumented thresholds in later practice.
evidenceBoundaries.allowedUse: Use to identify a course-design gap within the reviewed deliveries.

evidenceBoundaries.claim: The sponsor expects strategic assumptions to be reviewed during execution rather than only in the annual planning cycle.
evidenceBoundaries.observedScope: The approved brief and follow-up design conversation for this course revision
evidenceBoundaries.known: The requested change in review practice is explicit in the sponsor record.
evidenceBoundaries.uncertain: The organisation has not yet chosen one review cadence for every business unit.
evidenceBoundaries.allowedUse: Use to redesign the practice sequence while leaving local cadence choices open.

evidenceBoundaries.claim: A shared chain from diagnosis through revision can connect the preserved and changed parts of the course.
evidenceBoundaries.known: The existing work supplies diagnosis and choice while the new brief requires explicit review.
evidenceBoundaries.uncertain: The integrated chain still requires learner testing before wider use.
evidenceBoundaries.allowedUse: Use as the organising argument for this revision and test it through the carried record.

evidenceBoundaries.claim: The inherited diagnosis sequence remains necessary because later revision requires a baseline explanation.
evidenceBoundaries.known: A revision cannot be explained without knowing which original diagnosis it changes.
evidenceBoundaries.uncertain: The existing opening case may still need a lighter facilitation format.
evidenceBoundaries.allowedUse: Use to preserve the causal function while allowing minor delivery improvements.

evidenceBoundaries.claim: The inherited alternatives table should remain because explicit rejection makes later reopening interpretable.
evidenceBoundaries.known: The table already records selected and rejected options against a diagnosis.
evidenceBoundaries.uncertain: Its criteria may require adaptation for particular participant industries.
evidenceBoundaries.allowedUse: Use to retain the selection mechanism while adding an evidence threshold.

evidenceBoundaries.claim: Combining implementation teaching with participant cases can attach revision evidence directly to coordinated action.
evidenceBoundaries.known: The two inherited components currently use separate artifacts despite contributing to one final decision.
evidenceBoundaries.uncertain: The combined session timing must be tested with a live cohort.
evidenceBoundaries.allowedUse: Use to combine the two components while preserving an optional timing reserve.

carriedProof.name: Revisable Strategy Record
carriedProof.initialState: A strategic aspiration accompanied by initiatives but no explicit revision condition
carriedProof.finalState: A causal diagnosis, selective choice, coordinated actions, assumptions, and revision thresholds in one record
carriedProof.successEvidence: A reviewer can trace why the strategy was chosen and which evidence would reopen the choice.

capabilityProgression.learnerMove: Learners replace an aspiration with a causal account of the obstacle.
capabilityProgression.proofAdded: The record states the obstacle, mechanism, and evidence supporting the diagnosis.
capabilityProgression.handoff: A defensible diagnosis creates criteria for strategic choice.

capabilityProgression.learnerMove: Learners select one option and record why plausible alternatives remain rejected.
capabilityProgression.proofAdded: The record compares one selected and two rejected alternatives against explicit criteria.
capabilityProgression.handoff: The selected option now needs coordinated actions and revision evidence.

capabilityProgression.learnerMove: Learners attach reinforcing actions, assumptions, and review thresholds to their strategic choice.
capabilityProgression.proofAdded: The final record links each action to the choice and names evidence that would reopen it.
capabilityProgression.handoff: The record is ready for use in an operating review.

approval.provenance: The author and sponsor approved the hybrid architecture after reviewing the item-level transformation audit.

productionDecision.nextAction: Revise the six session plans around the approved Revisable Strategy Record.
